output.draft_reply:
Hi Dana,

thanks for the details. A 401 with error.code token_expired means the access token was valid but has reached the end of its lifetime. Fernwick access tokens expire 60 minutes after they are issued, so a worker that fetches a token only once at startup will start failing about an hour later.

To fix this, cache the token and refresh it about 5 minutes before expires_in runs out. If a call still returns 401 with token_expired, refresh once and retry that call once, rather than retrying in a loop.

Best regards,
Fernwick Support
output.reason: Customer reports 401 token_expired with a token fetched once at startup; the auth sections explain the 60-minute lifetime and refresh behaviour.

Hi Aiko,

thanks for the event ID. A webhook delivery only counts as successful when your endpoint returns a 2xx status within 10 seconds. Because your endpoint looks up the invoice before responding, which takes 15-20 seconds, deliveries time out and are treated as failed.

Please have the endpoint respond with 2xx first and process the event afterwards. Failed deliveries are retried with backoff for up to 72 hours, and you can replay events from the last 30 days from Dashboard > Developers > Webhooks > Delivery log. Events may arrive more than once, so deduplicate by event ID.

Best regards,
Fernwick Support

output.draft_reply:
Hi Tom,

a 403 means the request was authenticated, but the API key is not allowed to perform this action, which is why refreshing the token did not help. The error.code insufficient_scope with required_scope invoices:write means the key is missing the invoices:write scope that POST /v1/invoices needs.

A workspace admin can add this scope to the key in Dashboard > Developers > API keys. After that, creating invoices with the same key should work.

Best regards,
Fernwick Support
